main_issue: The canonical-path containment mechanism is coherent for the evidenced DSpace, S3Proxy, and likely JClouds filesystem cases, but the assigned group mixes distinct mechanisms including server-side URL fetching and unsafe inline file serving; several path-traversal labels have only review-entry anchors and no source-to-sink evidence.
suggested_guideline: Split this group into a filesystem containment guideline: trace attacker-controlled container names, object keys, upload identifiers, archive entry names, or path fragments into filesystem path resolution and file read/write/delete/list operations. Report paths where a resolved and normalized path can escape the intended tenant, container, upload, or extraction root before the sensitive operation. Require containment to be enforced on the exact resolved path used by the sink, including temporary-file derivations. Safely resolve against a fixed trusted base, normalize or canonicalize as appropriate for the filesystem semantics, reject paths outside that base, and apply equivalent checks to every read, write, delete, list, and permission-management path.
split_suggestions: Filesystem traversal and archive/upload extraction: attacker-controlled path components reach filesystem operations without normalized containment under a trusted root.
Server-side outbound fetch (SSRF): caller-controlled URLs reach URL.openStream or equivalent network clients without destination, scheme, and address-policy validation.
Unsafe inline file delivery / stored XSS: downloadable stored content is served inline with attacker-influenced MIME or disposition handling and no safe inline allowlist.
evidence_notes: CVE-2022-31194 (DSpace) directly supports the filesystem mechanism: resumableIdentifier and chunk parameters contribute to a temporary path under upload.temp.dir without canonical containment.

CVE-2025-24961 (S3Proxy) directly supports the filesystem mechanism across list, get, put, delete, and access operations: caller-controlled blob keys or prefixes are resolved under a container root without normalized containment.

CVE-2025-32960 (CUBA REST API) is a separate response-content mechanism: it selects inline versus attachment and MIME handling for stored file streaming, rather than resolving attacker-controlled filesystem paths.
CVE-2026-3189 (sz-boot-parent) is an SSRF mechanism: request-derived URL material reaches Java URL.openStream; it should not remain in a path-containment group.

CVE-2024-57669, CVE-2025-24961 (JClouds), and CVE-2026-3188 have path-traversal labels but only review-entry provenance, so their exact source, sink, and missing guard need source-level confirmation before inclusion.
The structural data corroborates the split: primary_hcvr_purity is only 0.5185 and the cluster summary explicitly identifies unrelated outliers.
